source.title: Tokens-per-Parameter Coverage Is Critical for Robust LLM Scaling Law Extrapolation
source.authors: Joshua Shay Kricheli; Alexander Reid; Soumajyoti Sarkar; Venkata Gandikota; Paulo Shakarian

record.tranche_reason: The study tests scaling-law extrapolation and argues that collinear training designs can make fitted parameters ill-conditioned and predictions unreliable; it proposes that TPP diversity is needed for reliable estimation.
record.gate_note: The study measures held-out prediction quality for fitted loss-scaling laws and compares collinear with non-collinear training designs. It does not test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, downstream-task predictability, or architecture-shape effects. Results cited from other papers are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains about 1,900 small LLaMA-style models on collinear (fixed tokens-per-parameter, TPP) and non-collinear (N, D) grids. It fits four loss-scaling laws to each and shows, by proof and by holdout error, that the fitted coefficients and their extrapolations depend on the experimental design. This is a specific result that V7 holds and that V2 needs qualifying. Holdouts extend only about 1.4x beyond the training range in N and D. The study does not test whether loss follows a power law over orders of magnitude (V1), compute-optimal allocation (V3), shape (V4), other regimes (V5) or downstream tasks (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that fixed-TPP (collinear) designs make scale coefficients practically unidentifiable when the N- and D-exponents are close. Such fits look confident in training but extrapolate poorly off the training ray. Even 12 collinear rays do not fix this; 2D (N, D) coverage with enough TPP diversity does. Single-ray fits should report only the combined reduced coefficient ψ, not separate model-versus-data contributions. They state the effect holds across precision, laws and corpora, but softens on specialized corpora.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains its own small LLaMA-style models on five corpora and compares collinear and non-collinear experimental designs while fitting four scaling-law formalisms; it is not a direct reproduction of the original large-scale studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction quality depends on whether the training design is collinear or non-collinear, on TPP diversity, and on corpus; the authors report weaker budget-matched results on Cosmopedia and peS2o. Repeated-data conditioning also depends on whether the fit is in the saturated or unsaturated regime.
record.peer_reviewed: Accepted to the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
record.problems: Empirical scope is limited to small models (5.04–76.5M parameters), one LLaMA-style architecture, English text, and a fixed training recipe. The authors note weaker budget-matched results on Cosmopedia and peS2o. The 30-seed confidence intervals vary the curve-fitting optimizer, not the underlying training data or runs. The preliminary higher-TPP result has a wide CI including 50%.
record.rows_left_out: The individual dataset-law-epoch results in Appendix E, the BF16 per-law breakdowns, and most fitted-parameter entries in Appendix F are not separately listed; the aggregate tables, the condition-dependent Regime A subset results in Table 6, and the preliminary higher-TPP result are retained.

untested.parts: Whether loss follows a power law at all over several orders of magnitude. N spans only about 15x (5.04–76.5M) and D about 40x, and no alternative functional forms are compared.
Extrapolation by orders of magnitude. The holdouts lie at most about 1.4x beyond the training N and D.
Compute-optimal N/D allocation. IsoFLOP corruption under collinearity is argued but not measured as an allocation.
Depth and width vary across configurations but are not compared in a controlled way.
Whether the power-law form holds under repeated data, other modalities, fine-tuning or transfer. Repeated data appears only as one of the fitted laws.

missing.what: Per-dataset win rates on the collinear holdout: NC advantage at chance on RedPajama (50.3%) and Wikipedia (48.3%), overall 72.1%. Overall non-collinear-holdout win rate 98.7%.
Win rate by epoch (first 99.8%, second 97.6%, final 93.8%) and by corpus (C4 93.0% up to RedPajama 100%).

record.verdict_notes: Holdout and train losses are the mean of the final 100 batch training losses per epoch, not a separate validation set. The CIs reflect optimizer-seed variance only, with one training run per (N, D). N includes embeddings for all laws, including Kaplan. Appendix F shows large design-dependent exponent shifts (e.g. Wikipedia Chinchilla α 0.908 CO vs 0.260 NC). That would be direct V7 evidence, but the record declares it left out.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments cover model sizes 5.04–76.5M parameters and dataset sizes approximately 10M–401M tokens, not several orders of magnitude or training compute as an independently varied axis.
The held-out predictions extend beyond the training design but not by orders of magnitude to substantially larger models.
The study does not find loss-minimising parameter/token allocations under fixed compute or estimate their growth rates with compute.
Architecture configurations vary, but there is no controlled comparison isolating the effect of depth, width, or other shape choices on loss.
The study tests repeated-data training across epochs, but not image/video modalities, fine-tuning, transfer, or other training regimes.

The study examines design dependence and discusses fitting and counting conventions, but does not systematically sweep parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, datasets, and fitting methods independently.

relationships.condition: Collinear vs non-collinear designs; web-crawled corpora and the aggregate across four laws, five corpora and three epochs
relationships.reason: Holdout fit quality depends strongly on the sampling design. Unified-holdout R2 is 0.837 vs 0.932 and RMSE 0.237 vs 0.156. NC wins 97.3% of seed-paired comparisons (98.7% under BF16) and 72–88% of budget-matched comparisons on web corpora. Theory gives condition number Θ(ε⁻²) (r1, r2, r4–r6, r8–r11, r19–r21, r24, r26).
relationships.display_finding: Non-collinear sampling improved held-out R² from 0.837 to 0.932 and RMSE from 0.237 to 0.156, winning 97.3% of seed-paired comparisons, 98.7% under BF16 and 72–88% of budget-matched web-corpus comparisons, while theory gave condition-number scaling Θ(ε⁻²).

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Collinear vs non-collinear designs; web-crawled corpora and the aggregate across four laws, five corpora and three epochs
source_check.reason: The aggregate prediction differences and identifiability analysis support fitting-design dependence. The stated 72–88% budget-matched range applies to Chinchilla and Kaplan on web corpora; Droppo-Elibol is 62.2–67.2%.

relationships.condition: Specialized corpora (Cosmopedia, peS2o) in budget-matched comparisons; the collinear holdout; BF16; higher-TPP runs
relationships.reason: The design advantage vanishes on specialized corpora (45.5–51.8%) and is weaker for Droppo-Elibol (62–67%). It shrinks on the collinear holdout (0.911 vs 0.944) and under BF16 (0.941 vs 0.966), and is non-significant at higher TPP (63.3%, CI includes 50%) (r3, r7, r12–r18, r22, r23, r25).
relationships.display_finding: The design advantage vanished on specialized corpora (45.5–51.8%), weakened for Droppo-Elibol (62–67%), narrowed on the collinear holdout (0.911 versus 0.944) and under BF16 (0.941 versus 0.966), and was inconclusive at higher tokens per parameter (63.3%, with a confidence interval including 50%).
